record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.context_brief: Local normal forms for Nijenhuis operators
record.original_question: For a Nijenhuis operator L on a manifold M, what local normal form can L be brought to near almost every point after a local change of coordinates?

evidence.quote: (1) Local description: to what form can one bring a Nijenhuis operator near almost every point by a local coordinate change?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $L: TM \to TM$ be a smooth $(1,1)$-tensor field on $M$. The Nijenhuis torsion of $L$ is the $(1,2)$-tensor $\mathcal{N}_L$ defined by
$$\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y) = L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY]$$
for all vector fields $X, Y$ on $M$. The operator $L$ is called a Nijenhuis operator if $\mathcal{N}_L \equiv 0$.

Problem. Describe all local normal forms to which an arbitrary Nijenhuis operator $L$ can be reduced, in a neighborhood of almost every point $p \in M$ (i.e., on an open dense subset of $M$), by means of a smooth local change of coordinates. In other words, classify, up to local diffeomorphism, the germs of Nijenhuis operators at generic points of $M$.
artifact.category_tag: Nijenhuis operators and local normal forms
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a central open program in Nijenhuis geometry. Partial results provide local normal forms under additional regularity assumptions: gl-regular operators admit explicit canonical forms (theorems by Bolsinov–Konyaev–Matveev), algebraically generic operators with eigenvalues of geometric multiplicity one are classified, and Jordan-block normal forms with non-constant real eigenvalues are known. A complete local classification near almost every point — including all singular behavior — remains open and is listed among the open problems of the Nijenhuis geometry program.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis Geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Local normal forms are established for gl-regular Nijenhuis operators and under algebraic genericity assumptions, classifying canonical forms including Jordan blocks.
status_evidence.claim: Partial local normal forms are known under gl-regularity and algebraic genericity.
